injuryReport.name: Christian Benford
factors: Positive upward rehab ramp (Wed DNP -> Thu LP; player prior 76%)
injuryReport.beatComment: Benford is working through a groin injury that caused him to be sidelined for Sunday's win against the Dolphins. His return to practice is encouraging, even if it was in a limited capacity, and a full session Wednesday would put the fifth-year pro on track to return for Thanksgiving Day against the Chiefs. If Benford cannot play Thursday, then the Bills would likely elevate Tre'Davious White from the practice squad and rotate him with Maxwell Hairston at outside cornerback opposite Davison Igbinosun.

injuryReport.name: Dorian Williams
factors: Thursday Limited Participation (LP); player toughness prior = 81%
injuryReport.beatComment: Williams did not play in Sunday's win over the Dolphins due to a calf injury that kept him out of all Week 11 prep. The inside linebacker's estimated presence Monday is promising, but he will likely need to suit up for on-field work Tuesday and Wednesday to get the green light ahead of Thursday night's Thanksgiving showdown with the Chiefs.

injuryReport.name: O'Cyrus Torrence
factors: Thursday Limited Participation (LP); player toughness prior = 81%

injuryReport.name: Dalton Kincaid
factors: Thursday Limited Participation (LP); player toughness prior = 78%
injuryReport.beatComment: Kincaid, who was inactive for this past Sunday's win over the Dolphins, logged a 'limited' listing on the Bills' Monday through Wednesday practice/injury reports before being deemed 'questionable' to face Kansas City. Per Matt Parrino of The Syracuse Post-Standard, following Tuesday's practice Kincaid said that he's "most likely playing" Thursday, with the tight end's Week 12 status, either way, set to be confirmed once Buffalo's scratches are posted ahead of the team's 8:20 pm kickoff.

injuryReport.name: T.J. Sanders
factors: Thursday Limited Participation (LP); player toughness prior = 81%

injuryReport.name: Greg Rousseau
injuryReport.beatComment: Rousseau was limited in Monday's session while managing a back injury, but his full participation Tuesday indicates that the sixth-year edge rusher will be available against the Chiefs on Thanksgiving Day. Rousseau logged two sacks against the Dolphins on Sunday, and his 10.0 sacks through 10 regular-season games are second-most in the NFL behind Will Anderson (11.5).

injuryReport.name: Amani Hooker
injuryReport.beatComment: Hooker has now played in two games for the Bills, logging 100 percent of the team's defensive reps in Week 11 and 98 percent in Week 12. The strong safety has made for a good pairing with Cole Bishop, and the duo has helped the Bills' defense extend its streak of not allowing a touchdown to 15 straight quarters of play.

injuryReport.name: Ty Johnson
injuryReport.beatComment: Johnson did not carry the rock much at all in the contest. The running back did, however, rank third in receiving yards for Buffalo behind Khalil Shakir (101) and DJ Moore (91). Johnson should continue to see receiving opportunities in Week 12 against the Chiefs as the Bills' preferred third-down back.

injuryReport.name: Ed Oliver
injuryReport.beatComment: Oliver popped up on the injury report after informing the team's medical staff of oblique pain and was listed as questionable. However, the veteran is cleared to play for Sunday's divisional meeting with Miami, potentially resulting in fewer snaps for DeWayne Carter, Greg Gaines and Landon Jackson.

injuryReport.name: Jackson Hawes
injuryReport.beatComment: Hawes was in danger of missing this contest due to a shoulder issue, though he will avoid his first absence of the 2026 campaign Sunday versus Miami. With Dalton Kincaid (thumb) sidelined in Week 11, Hawes will have an opportunity to get more involved than usual behind Dawson Knox.

coachingMatchup.headline: Andy Reid & DC Steve Spagnuolo vs. HC Joe Brady, OC Pete Carmichael Jr. & DC Jim Leonhard (Road Test)
coachingMatchup.summary: Week 12 two-sided coordinator chess match pitting Kansas City Chiefs's staff (Andy Reid, OC Eric Bieniemy, DC Steve Spagnuolo) against Buffalo Bills (9-1)—testing both Kansas City's offensive efficiency and its defensive pass-rush and coverage discipline.
bullets: Pass-Game Efficiency & Coverage Shell Delta: Andy Reid and OC Eric Bieniemy pair condensed splits with pre-snap jet motion and orbit motion to stress Buffalo Bills's single-high vs. two-high rotations—widening curl/flat defenders to attack the honey-hole between hook/curl linebackers and deep safeties on play-action choice/dagger concepts.

Trench Run-Fit & Two-Way Leverage: Against Buffalo Bills's pin-and-pull, counter, and duo runs targeting the A- and B-gaps, DC Steve Spagnuolo balances four-man pressure with disguised Quarters and Cover 6 split-safety rotations on early downs and in the red zone.

Money-Down & Red-Zone Execution: Third-down conversion discipline and red-zone touchdown rate govern whether Kansas City sustains multi-play scoring drives or yields momentum to Buffalo Bills's pass rush and coverage disguises.
Tempo, Turnovers & Venue Leverage: Road Test situational play-calling, penalty margin, and turnover differential provide the clearest late-game swing factors for both coaching staffs.

keyMatchupsMatrix.unitMatchup: Patrick Mahomes, Travis Kelce & Xavier Worthy vs. S Amani Hooker & LB Greg Rousseau
keyMatchupsMatrix.statComparison: KC: #4 Pass Off (262.7 yds) · #6 Off. Scoring (+7.92) | BUF: #7 Pass Def (-1.36)
keyMatchupsMatrix.tacticalDetail: Patrick Mahomes, Travis Kelce & Xavier Worthy attack the intermediate seams and middle-of-the-field leverage windows against Buffalo Bills's #7 pass defense (-1.36). Winning early-down timing throws keeps Kansas City's offense ahead of the chains and punishes disguised single-high rotations.
keyMatchupsMatrix.filmTell: Watch Patrick Mahomes (#15) scanning Bills's deep safeties at the snap—when LB Greg Rousseau widens to take away the crossers, the intermediate seam opens immediately for Travis Kelce (#87).

keyMatchupsMatrix.unitMatchup: George Karlaftis, Chris Jones & Ashton Gillotte vs. QB Josh Allen & OT Dion Dawkins
keyMatchupsMatrix.statComparison: KC: #16 Def Sacks (2.3/gm) | BUF: #16 Pass Protection (6.5%)
keyMatchupsMatrix.tacticalDetail: George Karlaftis, Chris Jones & Ashton Gillotte lead Kansas City's #16 NFL pass rush (2.3/gm) against Buffalo Bills's #16 pass-protection unit (6.5%). Collapsing the interior pocket without sending extra blitzers lets Chiefs keep seven defenders in coverage.
keyMatchupsMatrix.filmTell: On 3rd-and-6+, watch whether George Karlaftis (#56) draw chip help from Bills's tight ends or backs—creating 1-on-1 rush lanes inside for Chris Jones (#95).

keyMatchupsMatrix.unitMatchup: Nick Bolton, Chamarri Conner & Nohl Williams vs. WR DJ Moore & QB Josh Allen
keyMatchupsMatrix.statComparison: KC: #6 Pass Def (-2.69) | BUF: #12 Pass Off (241.6 yds)
keyMatchupsMatrix.tacticalDetail: Nick Bolton, Chamarri Conner & Nohl Williams anchor Kansas City's #6 pass defense (-2.69) against WR DJ Moore and Buffalo Bills's #12 passing attack (241.6 yds). Limiting explosive 20+ yard chunk plays forces Bills into sustained red-zone drives.
keyMatchupsMatrix.filmTell: Track Nick Bolton (#32) at the top of routes against WR DJ Moore: press-bail alignment with safety help over the top takes away QB Josh Allen's preferred isolation shots.

keyMatchupsMatrix.unitMatchup: Emmett Johnson & Josh Downs vs. Bills Front Seven & LB Greg Rousseau
keyMatchupsMatrix.statComparison: KC: #5 Rush Off (134.2 yds) | BUF: #22 Rush Def (-0.16)
keyMatchupsMatrix.tacticalDetail: Emmett Johnson & Josh Downs test Buffalo Bills's #22 run defense (-0.16) with horizontal stretch and interior cutback lanes. Generating 4.5+ yards on first down unlocks play-action explosives and neutralizes Bills's pass-rush packages.
keyMatchupsMatrix.filmTell: Watch whether Bills's linebackers over-pursue motion to the perimeter—opening decisive backside B-gap cutback lanes for Emmett Johnson (#10).

keyMatchupsMatrix.unitMatchup: Creed Humphrey, Kahlil Benson & Trey Smith vs. DT T.J. Sanders & Bills Simulated Pressures
keyMatchupsMatrix.statComparison: KC: #16 Pass Protection (6.0%) | BUF: #16 Def Sacks (2.4/gm)
keyMatchupsMatrix.tacticalDetail: Creed Humphrey, Kahlil Benson & Trey Smith protect Patrick Mahomes (#16 protection at 6.0%) against DT T.J. Sanders and Buffalo Bills's #16 pass rush (2.4/gm). Passing off interior twists and simulated blitzes cleanly determines late-down conversion efficiency.
keyMatchupsMatrix.filmTell: Watch Creed Humphrey (#52) on obvious passing downs—if DT T.J. Sanders cannot win clean around the arc, Bills must dial up interior stunts that stress Kahlil Benson (#70).
